business_question: Can a small model answer from supplied evidence and decline to invent an answer when the evidence is missing?
conclusion: The model passed 11 of 12 reserved checks and all three critical cases, meeting this demonstration benchmark. It improved missing-evidence responses and avoided selecting an answer from unresolved conflicting notices. The original already answered six cases correctly and recognised missing information in two more but failed the prescribed abstention format, so part of the gain is output discipline. The trained model still omitted reception from a collection location. Passing these 12 synthetic cases does not establish production reliability or authorise a live release.
